note: Menu Item Fields makes the menu_link_content entity type fieldable and renderable with view modes. Fields attach to the single bundle menu_link_content (entity_type=menu_link_content, bundle=menu_link_content). Menus render through a block plugin 'menu_item_fields' ('Menu with fields', derived per menu) with settings view_mode and view_mode_override_field. Per-menu form modes are auto-used when a menu_link_content form mode's machine name matches the menu (dashes->underscores). The menu_item_fields_ui submodule provides Field UI for menu links. No configure route/permission/schema/Drush. Medium/hard cases create namespaced fields (field_mif_*) and view modes (mif_*) on menu_link_content and inspect/verify them.

evals.prompt: What does the Drupal contrib module menu_item_fields make fieldable, and how do you actually render a menu so those extra fields show up?
evals.expected_output: It makes the menu_link_content entity type fieldable. You render the menu with the block it provides, 'Menu with fields' (block plugin id menu_item_fields, derived per menu), which renders each menu_link_content entity through the entity view builder using a chosen view mode.

evals.prompt: I enabled menu_item_fields but I don't see any way to add fields to my menu links. What do I need to enable, and what does it do?
evals.expected_output: Enable the menu_item_fields_ui submodule. It wires Field UI to the menu_link_content entity (sets its field_ui_base_route to entity.menu.collection and defaults the bundle to menu_link_content on the field routes), so Manage fields / form & view displays appear under Menus. Like Field UI it can be disabled in production afterward.

evals.prompt: The 'Menu with fields' block from menu_item_fields has two extra settings beyond a normal menu block. What are they, and what do per-menu form modes let you do?
evals.expected_output: The block has view_mode (the menu_link_content view mode used to render items) and view_mode_override_field (a field on the menu link naming a per-item view-mode id). Per-menu form modes: create/enable a menu_link_content form mode whose machine name matches a menu (dashes->underscores) and menu_item_fields uses it when editing that menu's links.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, a custom field has been added to menu links (the menu_link_content entity). Inspect the live configuration and give the machine name of that field.
evals.expected_output: The field is field_mif_known: there is a FieldConfig menu_link_content.menu_link_content.field_mif_known (with a matching field storage on the menu_link_content entity type).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, a custom view mode has been configured for menu links (the menu_link_content entity) so menus can render them differently. Inspect the live configuration and name that view mode's machine id.
evals.expected_output: The view mode is mif_mega: there is an entity view mode menu_link_content.mif_mega and an enabled entity_view_display menu_link_content.menu_link_content.mif_mega.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, using menu_item_fields, add a text (string) field with machine name field_mif_task to custom menu links (the menu_link_content entity), so editors can store an extra value on each menu item. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Create a FieldStorageConfig (entity_type menu_link_content, field_name field_mif_task, type string) and a FieldConfig on bundle menu_link_content. Verify checks that FieldConfig menu_link_content.menu_link_content.field_mif_task exists.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, using menu_item_fields, create a new view mode with machine name mif_hero for menu links (menu_link_content) and enable an entity view display for it, so the 'Menu with fields' block could render menu items in that view mode. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Create an EntityViewMode menu_link_content.mif_hero and an enabled EntityViewDisplay menu_link_content.menu_link_content.mif_hero (status true). Verify checks the view display exists and is enabled.
